tool_args.rationale: The provided signatures and rows are consistent with an input-saturating base flux, multiplicative sink inhibition, and an open signed square-root branch. Fit the candidate parameters numerically and rely on the required fresh confirmation to test the mechanistic choice.

considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: Gradient spans 0.25–2.2 already, exposing sink inhibition; measured response also supports a signed local branch term, so extra branch probe is not needed to identify this 3-parameter candidate.

All five observations share H=0.6 and vary instantaneous input and gradient; the pilot identifies base-field and sink-gradient signatures, not trajectory-dependent memory. ODE candidate is inapplicable and unnecessarily costly.

Both are plausible 4-parameter alternatives, but supplied C1/C2 monotone-concave signatures and observed rise/fall as gradient changes at varying input point toward the simpler two-layer siphon. Existing gradient spread is ample.
